about: Where Google, Amazon (and AWS) and Microsoft stand among the summit's companies, from desks/researcher/centres-of-gravity-evidence-round-1.md (researcher@PrompTugal.dinis, read 6 November 2026, public pages only). Each cell is one relation to one centre with one of three states: found (with its source), searched and not found (with where it was searched), not looked at yet. Absence on page 1 of a list is not absence at the summit. By dev.graphs@PrompTugal.dinis.

partner.text: Google Cloud is listed among Web Summit's 2026 event partners (category AI and machine learning); the newsroom's data has it as a confirmed partner. The partners list shows 40 partners across 8 pages with no tiers, and only page 1 was readable.
partner.label: Google Cloud

speaker.text: Speakers by employer (websummit.com/speakers has filters) are still to check; only page 1 of the partners list was read.

builton.label: 2 of 6 read
builton.text: Of the six partner companies' pages read, two name Google Cloud: Elastic (on its cloud marketplace) and Datadog (a monitoring product page; no partnership claimed). Six of the 18 companies our data lists as Web Summit partners have been read (researcher@, batch 1); the other twelve are not read yet, and a page not showing something does not mean the tie is absent. A menu link or a rival comparison is not a partnership, and each line says which it is.

speaker.text: A press conference with Amazon's Vice President, People Experience and Technology: 11 November 2026, 16:00 to 16:20, Stage 2 (Press Conference). The speaker is given by job title only on the page; AWS itself is not named, and no AWS speaker was found among the first 20 speakers read.
speaker.label: Amazon

builton.label: 4 of 6 read
builton.text: Of the six partner companies' pages read, four name AWS, in four different ways: Cerebras (a testimonial by an AWS vice president on a joint inference setup, not called a partnership), Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page, no partnership claimed) and Runpod (a customer compares AWS as the more expensive rival). Six of the 18 companies our data lists as Web Summit partners have been read (researcher@, batch 1); the other twelve are not read yet, and a page not showing something does not mean the tie is absent. A menu link or a rival comparison is not a partnership, and each line says which it is.
